High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The instant Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant seeking enhancement of the compensation amount by challenging the impugned Award dated 12.01.2018 passed by the Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (in short "the Claims Tribunal") in Motor Accident Claim Case No.6400246/2016.

entities.text: Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Along with the appeal, the appellants have filed I.A. No. 2762 of 2019, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay in filing the present appeal.
As per the office report, there is a delay of 446 days in filing the appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the impugned Award was pronounced on 12.01.2018 and the appellant applied for a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10636 2 MA-3698-2019 certified copy of the same on 15.01.2018, which was made available on 23.01.2018.

The appellant had been diligently pursuing the matter and had bona fide relied upon the assurance given by his then counsel that the appeal would be filed within the prescribed period of limitation.
Learned counsel further submitted that due to an inadvertent and bona fide mistake on the part of the earlier counsel, the appeal could not be presented within the stipulated time.
The appellant was kept under the impression that necessary steps had already been taken.

It was only on 07.07.2019,
upon making enquiries, that the appellant came to know that the appeal had not been filed.

Ashutosh Sharma vs Pooran Singh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71536106/
1
Immediately thereafter, the appellant contacted another counsel, got the appeal prepared without any undue delay, and the same was filed before this Court on 08.07.2019.
Thus, there was no negligence or lack of diligence on the part of the appellant.

It is submitted that the delay in filing the appeal for the period from 21.04.2018 to 08.07.2019 is neither intentional nor deliberate, but has occurred due to circumstances beyond the control of the appellant.
The appellant should not be penalized for the bona fide lapse of his counsel.

In view of the above facts and in the interest of substantial justice, learned counsel prays that this Court may graciously be pleased to condone the delay in filing the appeal and allow the application, so that the matter may be adjudicated on merits.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company opposes the application for condonation of delay and submits that there is an inordinate delay of 446 days, which has not been satisfactorily explained.
The plea of mistake on the part of earlier counsel is vague and cannot constitute NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10636 3 MA-3698-2019 sufficient cause under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The appellant has failed to show due diligence and has not explained the delay day-to-day.
The law of limitation cannot be relaxed on such bald assertions.
Condonation of delay would prejudice the respondent as the Award has attained finality.
Hence, the application deserves to be dismissed.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
The law regarding condonation of delay is well-settled.

While a liberal approach is generally adopted in matters arising from the Motor Vehicles Act, being a social welfare legislation, the term "sufficient cause"
cannot be expanded to the extent of rendering the Law of Limitation redundant.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy, (2013) 12 SCC 649, observed that "the concept of liberal approach has to encapsulate the conception of adjudication of disputes on merits and not to enable a party to take the law for granted.

entities.text: Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy, (2013) 12 SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lack of bona fides imputable to a party seeking condonation of delay is a significant and relevant fact."

Similarly, in the matter of Postmaster General v. Living Media India Ltd., (2012) 3 SCC 563, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that in the absence of a plausible and acceptable explanation, the delay cannot be condoned mechanically.

entities.text: Postmaster General v. Living Media India Ltd., (2012) 3 SCC 563
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the present case, this Court finds that the delay of 446 days in filing the appeal has not been satisfactorily explained.
The explanation offered by the appellant is general and vague and does not account for the entire period of delay in a cogent and convincing manner.

Mere reliance on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10636 4 MA-3698-2019 the alleged lapse of earlier counsel, without any supporting material, cannot be accepted as "sufficient cause" under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The appellant has failed to demonstrate due diligence or bona fide conduct in pursuing the remedy within the prescribed period.
Even though the matter arises under the Motor Vehicles Act, a beneficial legislation, the law of limitation cannot be ignored altogether.

In the absence of a plausible and acceptable explanation covering the whole period of delay, this Court is of the considered opinion that sufficient cause has not been made out for condonation of delay.

Ashutosh Sharma vs Pooran Singh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71536106/
2 9.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court finds that the appellant has failed to establish sufficient cause for condoning the delay of 446 days in filing the appeal.
10. Accordingly, I.A. No. 2762 of 2019 filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay is dismissed.
Consequently, as the application for condonation of delay stands dismissed, the present Miscellaneous Appeal also stands dismissed as barred by limitation.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
